simple: This page explains the big ideas behind keeping your game safe from cheaters. The most important rule is: never trust the client, meaning the player's own device. Cheaters can change anything on their own computer, so the server must check every important action. If you plan for cheaters from the start, your game stays fair for everyone.
analogy: The server is like a bank teller and the client is like a customer. A customer can say "I have 1,000 dollars, give me 500", but the teller checks the real account balance before handing over any money.
keyPoints: Never trust the client. Assume anything a player's device sends could be faked.
Cheaters can read your LocalScripts and ModuleScripts that get sent to them, even ones that never run on their device.
Cheaters can move their character anywhere, change their speed, fire Touched or ProximityPrompt events from far away, and fire RemoteEvents as often as they want with any values.
The server is the boss. It should hold the real values for money, prices, health, and progress.
The server's job: receive a request, check that it is allowed, do it, then send the result to players.
Example: to buy an item, the server checks the real price, the player's real money, and how close the player is to the shop.
Think about security when you design each feature, not after it is done.
Keep important scripts and data in ServerScriptService, not in ReplicatedStorage or Workspace where players can see them.

terms.client: The player's own device (phone, PC, console) running your game. LocalScripts run here.
terms.server: Roblox's computer that runs the game for everyone in that server. Normal Scripts run here, and players cannot change it.
terms.exploiter: A cheater who uses special tools to change how the game runs on their device.
terms.decompile: To turn a script that was sent to the player back into readable code, so a cheater can see how it works.
terms.network ownership: Which computer is in charge of the physics of a part. Players usually own their own character, so they can control how it moves.
terms.RemoteEvent / RemoteFunction: Objects that let the client and server send messages to each other. Cheaters can fire them with any values they want.
terms.validate: To check that a request makes sense and is allowed before doing it.
terms.authoritative: The official, real version. If the server is authoritative, its numbers win over anything the client says.
terms.replicate: To copy changes from the server to players' devices so everyone sees the same thing.
terms.threat model: Thinking ahead about how someone could abuse a feature, and what the worst result could be.
terms.replicated container: A place like ReplicatedStorage or Workspace whose contents get copied to every player's device.

example.title: Server checks a shop purchase
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (add a RemoteEvent named BuyItem to ReplicatedStorage and a Part named ShopCounter to Workspace)
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local buyItem = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BuyItem")
local shopCounter = Workspace:WaitForChild("ShopCounter")

-- The server keeps the real prices. The client never sends a price.
local PRICES = { BloxyCola = 10 }
local MAX_SHOP_DISTANCE = 15 -- studs

-- The server keeps each player's real money
local money = {}
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	money[player] = 50
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	money[player] = nil
end)

buyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemName)
	-- 1. Is the item name real?
	local price = PRICES[itemName]
	if typeof(itemName) ~= "string" or price == nil then
		return
	end
	-- 2. Is the player close enough to the shop?
	local character = player.Character
	local root = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not root or (root.Position - shopCounter.Position).Magnitude > MAX_SHOP_DISTANCE then
		return
	end
	-- 3. Do they have enough money?
	if (money[player] or 0) < price then
		return
	end
	-- All checks passed: the server updates the real money
	money[player] -= price
	print(player.Name, "bought", itemName, "and now has", money[player])
end)
explain: Prices and money live only on the server, so a cheater cannot change them.
When a player fires `BuyItem`, the server first checks the item name is real.
Next it checks the player's character is within 15 studs of the shop counter.
Then it checks the player has enough money.
Only if every check passes does the server take the money away.

watchOut: Letting the client send the price or the amount of money. Always look these up on the server.
Thinking a LocalScript check is enough. Cheaters can skip or change any client code.
Putting secret logic in ReplicatedStorage. Players can read it there; use ServerScriptService.
Forgetting rate limits. Ask what happens if a player fires your remote 1,000 times per second.
